title: Convert cold-start postmortem actions into PRD ramp-safety contracts and tenant budget apportionment
creator: Priya Nair
description: Translate the recent cold-start incident postmortem into concrete, testable PRD requirements that (1) define ramp-safety contracts for rolling capacity changes, (2) allocate tenant-level failover/burst budgets, and (3) add acceptance tests for canaryed traffic shepherding to prevent cascading cache-regeneration storms.
background: A high-severity outage on 2026-02-26 revealed a cascading cold-start effect where concurrent cache regen and autoscale policies caused transient tail-latency spikes and tenant-level QoS violations. Postmortem recommended a set of operational guardrails and a tenant apportionment model; this ticket converts those operational actions into product requirements and acceptance criteria so they ship with the next runtime release.
postmortem_findings: Simultaneous KV cache invalidations across many replicas led to regenerated KV load concentrated in a short window
Autoscaler reacted to token-backlog signals without rate-limiting ramp-up, causing multiple workers to rehydrate caches at once
No tenant-level emergency budget: a noisy tenant could exhaust burst pool leading to cross-tenant tail latency impact
Existing rollout gates did not include synthetic verification for cache-regen storms or tenant-level QoS checks
prd_changes: Define a Ramp-Safety Contract: maximum allowed parallel worker ramp rate per deployment and per-tenant cap; default = 2x worker/hour, configurable per-customer
Introduce Tenant Burst Budgets: a soft allocation model (burst tokens) that gates immediate allocation of spare capacity to a single tenant until verification checks pass
Traffic Shepherd Strategy: a rolling, canaryed traffic reweighting orchestrator that stages traffic increases and runs synthetic cache-regen probes before allowing full ramp
Add KV Cache Regen Throttle: runtime policy to spread regen work across time windows and prioritize under-provisioned tenants
Expose new PRD configuration knobs in Console: ramp_rate, tenant_burst_budget, shepherd_probe_window, and regen_priority_policy
Operator-visible metrics and dashboards: per-tenant ramp_rate_usage, burst_budget_balance, regen_throughput, and synthetic_probe_status
acceptance_criteria: Ramp Safety: Deploy a controlled rollout where worker count increases do not exceed the defined ramp_rate; verify with synthetic traffic that tail p99 latency stays under SLO during ramp
Tenant Budgets: Simulate a noisy tenant consuming 10x baseline traffic; validate that burst_budget_balance enforces soft throttling and other tenants maintain p95/p99 within SLA
Traffic Shepherding: Canary rollout performs synthetic cache-regen probes for N=3 requests and passes correctness + latency checks before opening full traffic; failures halt ramp and notify on-call
KV Regen Throttle: Under coordinated regen event (simulated cache invalidation across 50 replicas), regen_throughput must be distributed to avoid >30% p99 latency degradation for other tenants
Console Controls: Ramp knobs visible in the Console and editable by users with appropriate RBAC; changes are audit-logged
Observability: New metrics emit for at least 7 days of retention in staging and add alert thresholds to SRE runbooks
tasks: Draft PRD section describing ramp-safety contracts and tenant burst model
Work with ENG to specify API surface and runtime flags for ramp_rate and tenant_burst_budget
Define synthetic probe test harness and add to canary pipeline
Design Console UX for exposing and editing ramp knobs (design consult with DES)
Create acceptance test matrix and automation in CI (staging) for load and regen simulations
Coordinate with SRE to add metrics and runbook entries and schedule a tabletop review
